judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states only when the period begins and never says when it ends, an incomplete definition on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Condition IV.B of the same endorsement supplies the end date, so the gap is filled elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line, tied to 'suspension' of a rented covered location; 'fost' is an obvious scanning error for 'lost'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the 'suspension' and 'business income' definitions; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Untenantable for the purposes identified to the Insurer at the inception of the Policy' points outside the document to unspecified communications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Those purposes would come from the application, which IX.F makes a warranty, but nothing in the policy records them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A counterfactual start date for delayed operations, stated in one clear sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with the 'period of interruption' definition it modifies; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Remedied to the point at which normal operations could reasonably be restored' and the exclusion of losses from 'unfavorable business conditions caused by the impact of the covered pollution condition' are both open to competing readings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional appraisal mechanism; 'or any other amount that is or may be covered' is broader than 'business income' and blurs the scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A binding appraisal sits uneasily with the exclusive-jurisdiction condition and with the reservation in its own last sentence that the Insurer may still deny the claim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any of the individually excluded exposures identified above' has no clear antecedent — nothing is 'individually excluded' above it in this endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two dollar figures; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A catastrophe-specific retention of $100,000 duplicates the Coverage A/B retention without saying whether both apply to one event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In excess of the self-insured retention' does not say which retention, given that the endorsement creates its own; otherwise the grant is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $250,000 sublimit is expressly subordinated to the Declarations limits, but the retention ambiguity is a live cross-reference to Endorsement 4's own figure and to V.AA.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'right and the duty' to retain a consultant that is nevertheless subject to prior consent; workable but internally odd.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'National or regional news exposure ... reasonably likely to have a negative impact' on reputation or good will is vague at its edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds 'catastrophe management event' consistently; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'the good faith opinion of a key executive' plus a prediction that costs 'will exceed' the retention — a subjective trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other Endorsement 4 definitions and with V.AA; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined purely by the Insurer's written approval; definite though wholly discretionary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That unfettered approval right sits against IX.M's requirement that consent not be unreasonably withheld.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes advisory services in general terms ('minimizing potential harm', 'restoring public confidence') but the category is recognisable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the catastrophe management grant and cost definition; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 5 ends in 'or other necessary response costs' — an open catch-all after a list of specific personal-harm costs, the classic ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Requiring the Insurer's written approval for all such costs must be read with IX.M and the exclusion of legal defence expense; broadly coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of offices with a designation mechanism; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps but does not conflict with 'responsible person'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear consent requirement; the section is miscited as 'I1V.' and 'express' has been dropped from the consent standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces VII.C, so the policy carries two differently worded consent conditions and the reader must decide which governs remediation costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any of the individually excluded exposures identified above' again lacks an antecedent within the endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same defect as the parallel Endorsement 3 provision; the reference has to be supplied from Section VI by inference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule's retroactive dates are corrupted in the text ('11/01/2074', '41/01/2014', '11/07/2014'), and the coverage column heading is mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines which sites get Coverage A only versus A and B, and Item 8 also points to Endorsement 11, so the scope of 'covered location' depends on reading the two schedules together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a retroactive-date limb to Coverage A; the drafting is clear apart from stray comma placement in the reporting sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introductory sentence breaks off ('replaced with the'), and the substituted text silently drops 'legal defense expense' from the per-condition limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean aggregate statement, again describing Item 2.c as the Insurer's maximum liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2.c is $9,000,000 while the Item 4 Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000, so this 'maximum' cannot be the true ceiling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It limits the Coverage B per-condition limit to conditions 'resulting from covered operations', a term in quotation marks that the policy never defines.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same undefined quoted term 'covered operations' governs the Coverage B aggregate, narrowing it by reference to nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coverage B in Insuring Agreement I.B contains no 'covered operations' condition, so the limit provision and the grant do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated end-points for the defence duty; clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States erosion of both the dedicated sublimit and the Item 4 aggregate plus the retention; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with the capitalised notice that defence expenses erode limits and retention, and with Endorsement 6.III; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single figure subordinated to the Item 4 aggregate; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $2,000,000 defence sublimit sits inside a $7,000,000 total aggregate; consistent, though the defence-cost treatment differs between the base form and this endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The hammer sentence is broken — 'a settlement of any ongoing or future claim for which it is not which is acceptable to a claimant' — which obscures the condition being imposed, and 'covered loss' is an undefined quoted term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ninety days, no charge, one condition; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the printed sixty-day text in VIII.C, leaving two figures in the instrument, though the deletion language is explicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise durations and a premium cap; the only oddity is the misnumbered first condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supersedes VIII.D's thirty-four month version; the express deletion resolves it, but the two texts remain printed together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly scrambled — the replacement heading, the 'H.' paragraph and the definition are interleaved — and item 3 cross-refers to 'Subsection D., above' which does not precede it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 11.I also deletes Subsection F 'in its entirety' and substitutes a different list, so two endorsements each claim to supply the operative definition of 'covered location'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second paragraph piles up conditions on covered claims and the retroactive date is printed after the definition rather than within it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 11.II likewise deletes and replaces Subsection D 'Claim', so the definition is replaced twice with different limiting language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four cumulative provisos about permitting, bankruptcy, listing and remediation status, each objectively verifiable; long but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb 2 points to a Schedule of Disposal Sites Endorsement that is not attached, and the definition displaces V.U; otherwise coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two limbs, with limb 1 excluding conditions at sites that are 'not non-owned disposal sites' — a double negative that is workable but clumsy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear notice periods; the sentence limiting 2.b to the offending insured, followed by 'This exception shall not apply to any insured who is a parent corporation ... affiliated by ownership', is confusingly self-cancelling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds transportation as an alternative coverage trigger; clear, though it reinstates 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Movement 'by an insured, or by a person or entity ... engaged in the business of transporting property for hire', ending at unloading; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It occupies Subsection E, deleting 'contingent transportation', a term the base Vehicles exclusion still invokes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or other conveyance' remains an open catch-all after a specific list, but the carve-back for 'transportation' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with the replaced definition E and the replaced Insuring Agreement A in the same endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule is textually scrambled — bare numerals 1 to 9 sit apart from the named farms and the heading is embedded mid-list — so which entries are scheduled is not cleanly stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is garbled and the final carve-out — no claim 'from or made in relation to the owner, operator, contractor of the non-owned covered location; or those of their employees' — is broad and hard to bound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including smoke, soot, vapors ...' is the classic general-plus-specific pollution list, and the flat carve-out 'does not include any odor' sharpens the fight over what else counts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: By deleting the fungi limb it leaves the 'fungi' and 'certified industrial hygienist' definitions and the fungi fallback in 'remediation costs' with nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad concurrent-causation wording, and it excludes 'odor' — a term used but nowhere defined — alongside defined 'fungi'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It nullifies the fungi machinery elsewhere in the policy (definition L, the certified industrial hygienist, the fungi sentence in 'remediation costs'), which remain printed as though operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sublimit figure with a subordination sentence; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Natural resource damage is a limb of 'property damage', so a $500,000 cap carves a hole in the Coverage A and B limits, but the subordination language addresses that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three figures and a retroactive date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Endorsement 13.II's limits provision; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short sanctions clause using 'us' where the rest of the policy says 'the Insurer'; the substance is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses sanctions; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be reconciled on its face with the Jurisdiction and Venue condition's submission to the 'exclusive jurisdiction of the State of New York', and the two must be harmonised or one subordinated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other than as above stated' is precisely the phrase that decides whether the endorsement overrides or yields to the policy's forum condition — a self-referential qualifier with two readings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A signatures statement with a scanning artefact in the middle; nothing of substance to construe.
